newsitem.title: UK: London gold finds floor after early rise falters.
newsitem.headline: London gold finds floor after early rise falters.

text.p: Gold prices tested support on Wednesday afternoon after selling on Comex wiped out an earlier rise, dealers said.
"There was very heavy selling earlier and that encouraged people to get bullish when it was well absorbed," a dealer said.
However Comex turned lower when hopes of a prolonged rally began to fade.
At the fixing the Comex February contract had come back to $370.00, down $0.50 having been a dollar firmer earlier.
Gold was fixed at $368.25 per ounce after $369.60 earlier and $368.25 on Tuesday afternoon.
Dealers said $368.00 appeared to be the current support.
"Support looks to be available at $368.00," a dealer said, adding that the market had been encouraged by that to go modestly long in Europe.
However a break through $370.50 was needed to lead gold up to $373.00, he added.
Initial support for gold came from a weaker dollar and a turndown in London share prices, dealers said.
There was no evident benefit to gold from a 50-point lower opening on the Dow Jones Industrial average.
The market also ignored November core producer price index data showing a lower than forecast 0.1 percent rise. The headline rate was up 0.4, against a forecasts 0.3 percent rise.
Dealers said the market was caught slightly off guard overnight by the 0.50 percentage point cut in Australian interest rates to six percent.
The cut, the third in five months, reflected a further improvement in the domestic inflation outlook.
Inflation was likely to remain below 2.5 percent, according to an Australian central bank official.
"The lower Australian dollar might take some of the pressure off the producers to forward-sell gold," one dealer said.
But with operations already beginning to wind down ahead of the Christmas holiday and the approach of year-end, the market was likely to remain fairly thin and nervous, a dealer said.
The other metals moved with gold attracting support in the morning but coming off intraday highs after gold slid.
Silver which attracted some buying earlier was indicated at $4.78/$4.80 down two cents having made $4.89 bid earlier.
There was a lso light early buying of platinum but it had gomne back to $367.00/$369.00 down $0.50 after the gold fixing.
Palladium however held earlier gains to be indicated adollar firmer at $119.25/$120.25. -- Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
